import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Publish an agent, fork someone else's into your tenant, or call a published agent without forking it. A2A agent cards make public agents discoverable by other platforms.

A2A (Agent-to-Agent) is an open protocol for agents to find and call each other; an agent card is the public description an agent publishes. A fork is your private copy.

## What is the Marketplace

In the dashboard, **Marketplace** sits under the Workspace section. Two registries sit behind it:

- **Agent Marketplace**: published agents (`/v1/marketplace`). Filter by category or search text; star, fork, or unpublish your own. Listings carry a description, tags, README, star and fork counts.
- **MCP Marketplace**: a curated registry of Model Context Protocol servers (`/v1/mcp/servers`). Attach one to an agent with `POST /v1/agents/{name}/mcp-servers`.

<Aside>
A fork is a copy in your tenant. The original author does not see your data or runs.
</Aside>

## A2A agent cards and visibility

PAL implements the **Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol** for cross-platform agent discovery. Agents are **private by default** (`agents.is_public = false`). The card, the well-known directory, and A2A invoke only expose an agent to a non-owner when it is marked public.

<Aside type="caution">
No REST endpoint sets the flag yet; today it is a column on `agents` that an operator flips.
</Aside>

### Visibility rules

- An authenticated caller always sees and can invoke their **own** agents regardless of visibility.
- A card or invoke for another tenant's agent returns **404** (not 403) when the agent is not public, to avoid leaking that the agent exists.
- `GET /.well-known/agent.json` lists only `is_public = true` agents.

### Agent card endpoints

```http
GET /v1/agents/{name}/card          — own agent or is_public; else 404
GET /.well-known/agent.json          — lists only public agents
```

## Publishing your agent

Publishing copies the agent's manifest into the public registry under a slug. There is no review queue and no unlisted mode; a listing is live as soon as the call returns.

```http
POST /v1/marketplace/publish
{
  "agentName": "research-agent",
  "description": "Cited research reports",
  "category": "research",
  "tags": ["research", "web"],
  "readme": "..."
}

DELETE /v1/marketplace/{slug}     # unpublish
```

<Aside type="caution">
Anyone can read a published agent's manifest, including its system prompt. Do not put secrets in a manifest. Use `pal.secret/...` refs, which each tenant resolves from its own store at run time.
</Aside>

## Discovering and forking agents

```http
GET  /v1/marketplace?category=research&q=citations
GET  /v1/marketplace/{slug}                 # manifest, card, README
POST /v1/marketplace/{slug}/fork            { "newName": "my-copy" }
POST /v1/marketplace/{slug}/star
```

A fork is a normal agent in your tenant. Edit its prompt, swap models, add connectors; the original is unaffected.

## Cross-tenant invocation (commerce)

A buyer can invoke a published agent without forking it. The run executes in the **seller's** tenant, with their LLM keys and budgets. The seller's hard-fail budget applies (HTTP 402), and the buyer's input is validated against the manifest's `inputSchema` when one exists. The buyer gets the output and an HMAC-SHA256 signed receipt.

```http
POST /v1/marketplace/{slug}/invoke
{ "input": { "topic": "..." } }

Receipt fields: invocationId, buyerTenant, sellerTenant, marketplace,
  agentName, runId, costUsd, issuedAt, signature, algorithm

GET /v1/marketplace/invocations?role=buyer    # buyer-side history
GET /v1/marketplace/invocations?role=seller   # seller-side history
```

## Cross-platform interop

- **Discovery**: other platforms read `/.well-known/agent.json` and `/v1/agents/{name}/card`. Both are limited to public agents (plus your own, when authenticated).
- **Inbound call**: `POST /v1/agents/{name}/a2a/invoke` requires an authenticated caller; it returns 401 without credentials.
- **Outbound call**: inside a running agent, `ctx.a2a(agentCardUrl).submit({ input })` calls a remote A2A agent through the runtime sidecar (production runtime only). `ctx.subagent(name, input)` calls another agent by name.
